method: 50 exact distinct host article pages opened through direct URL and relevant presentation/commentary text checked. Distinguishes direct article passage inspection from complete panel and critical-edition review.

rows.selectedSourceObservation: The Nancy–Toul and Saint-Dié presentation gives different historical diocesan Missal propers for Saint Epvre and says both local dates moved to 17 September in 1962.
The presentation distinguishes St John Leonardi's universal 1940 inscription from the more prominent Saint Denis celebration in France; a 2009 Benedict XVI catechesis is reproduced.
The 31 May Queenship of Mary feast is credited to Pius XII in 1954; the page reproduces Lefebvre's theological reflection on Marian Queenship.

rows.articleTitle: Mardi de la 2ᵉ semaine de l’Avent
rows.selectedSourceObservation: The Advent Tuesday commentary by Guéranger expounds Lucifer, sin, and the awaited Messianic reversal with the repeated Latin Advent antiphon.

rows.articleTitle: Vendredi de la 2ᵉ semaine de l’Avent
rows.selectedSourceObservation: Guéranger's Friday Advent meditation treats the world's spiritual preparation, while Schuster explicitly redirects the weekday Mass discussion to Sunday.

rows.articleTitle: Samedi de la 2ᵉ semaine de l’Avent
rows.selectedSourceObservation: Guéranger treats Mary's bearing of Christ as an Advent preparation, and the Schuster entry redirects the Missal commentary to the second Advent Sunday.
The local Translation of Saint Mansuy carries three proper prayers and a shorter Sadducees Gospel passage distinct from the saint's ordinary feast.
The host confirms suppression of the Sacred Heart octave in 1955 and supplies Chanoine Reck commentary keyed to a different pre-1929 Sacred Heart Mass.
Presentation introduces Nicholas of Tolentino; the hosted Salesian excerpt is a dated 10 September 1620 sermon for clothing and profession.
The page title is incorrectly 'Navigation', while its dated body concerns the 26 April Saints Clet and Marcellinus, and distinguishes Clet from the abolished Anaclet date.
The Eleutherius source distinguishes the Liber Pontificalis deposition date from later calendrical martyr status.
Source for Saint Margaret of Scotland includes the same historical presentation and Guéranger commentary as a0514_ancien; the five panel hashes match exactly.
The local Saint Augustin Schoeffler account follows his Nancy upbringing, priestly ordination and mission to Tonkin, with an account of persecution.
The Wenceslas source contains a Benedict XVI homily from 28 September 2009 rather than a nineteenth-century Missal commentary.

rows.articleTitle: St Placide et ses Compagnons, martyrs
rows.selectedSourceObservation: The site's introductory note distinguishes a fourth-century Sicilian martyr cult from a Benedictine identification with Benedict's disciple Placid, recorded from the twelfth century.

rows.articleTitle: Sts Denis, évêque, Rustique et Eleuthère, martyrs
rows.selectedSourceObservation: Saint Denis, Rusticus and Eleutherius appear as a universal commemoration but locally receive principal Mass in French dioceses; source rejects ninth-century Denis–Areopagite conflation.

rows.articleTitle: Sᵗᵉ Marguerite d’Ecosse, reine et veuve
rows.selectedSourceObservation: Second St Margaret of Scotland article duplicates all five exact normalized body hashes from a0184_nouveau.
Saint Joseph the Worker, instituted in 1955, receives editorial criticism of pastoral liturgical reform and a separate positive Lefebvre exposition.

rows.articleTitle: St Léonard de Port-Maurice, conf. (messe en certains lieux, suppl. du Missel)
rows.selectedSourceObservation: Saint Leonard of Port Maurice is explicitly marked Mass 'in some places'; the first biography passage describes youthful pilgrimages and devotional activity.

rows.articleTitle: 6ᵉ jour dans l’Octave de la Toussaint
rows.selectedSourceObservation: Sixth day of All Saints octave is identified as suppressed in 1955; Guéranger contrasts Mozarabic and Eastern funeral Alleluia traditions.
Saint Airy of Verdun is explicitly diocesan; the host invokes Fortunatus and Gregory of Tours for early testimony but also narrates a later baptism anecdote.
The former Sacred Heart octave day was abolished in 1955; website reproduces Pius XI's 1928 Miserentissimus Redemptor as historical devotional source.

rows.articleTitle: Vigile de la fête de tous les Saints
rows.selectedSourceObservation: The All Saints vigil page says the vigil was abolished in 1955 while preserving the former Mass and Guéranger penitential preparation.
The website itself says historians dispute the historical existence of Felix of Valois and notes late appearance in Trinitarian foundation accounts.
Saint Goëry is a St Dié particular feast, and the host says he was also kept in Nancy–Toul before 1955; the narrative includes local Epinal cult.
Euchaire's Nancy–Toul page narrates a Lorraine family of four saints and a particular 1955 calendar revision, also repeated in Libaire and Menne pages.
Libaire's St Dié/Nancy page reuses the Toul-family persecution narrative and differentiates the local calendars before and after 1955.
Menne's local St Dié/Nancy article repeats the four-siblings Toul story, distinguishing the virgin's peaceful death from the three martyr siblings.
Saint Arbogast source is explicitly Strasbourg diocesan and even labels his woodland eremitic life legendary while discussing regional monastic foundations.
Saint Gengoult's local history narrates a water ordeal in a marriage tale; the source's presentation identifies a regional Lorraine cult.
The Saint Lawrence octave existed historically but was removed in 1955; source contrasts much earlier calendars and old octave-day readings.

rows.articleTitle: 30 décembre (6ᵉ jour dans l’Octave de la Nativité)
rows.selectedSourceObservation: December 30 is described as sixth day of the Nativity octave; Guéranger relates Christmas and its feasts of companion saints.
Saint Louis article is a French proper and offers two Salesian draft sermon plans not actually written out by the saint.
The page says Saint Amon, second bishop of Toul, was celebrated in Nancy–Toul only until 1955 and discusses sources stemming from Adson.

rows.articleTitle: Commun d’un Martyr Pontife hors du Temps Pascal Sacerdótes Dei
rows.selectedSourceObservation: Dom Pius Parsch comments on Common of a Bishop Martyr Sacerdotes Dei and its scriptural consolation motif; identical normalized body to a0322_ancien.

rows.articleTitle: Commun d’un Martyr non Pontife hors du Temps Pascal Lætábitur iustus
rows.selectedSourceObservation: Parsch comments on Common of a non-bishop Martyr Laetabitur iustus, identical normalized body to a0324_ancien.

rows.articleTitle: Commun d’un Confesseur non Pontife Iustus ut palma
rows.selectedSourceObservation: Parsch contrasts two formulas for a non-bishop confessor, servant awaiting master and ascetic renunciation.
Parsch develops the Common of a non-martyr woman including themes of marriage, widowhood and Martha/Mary.

rows.articleTitle: Messes de la Sᵗᵉ Vierge le Samedi I Avent
rows.selectedSourceObservation: Advent Saturday Mass of the Blessed Virgin contains a historical common Saturday-Marian introduction reused across all five seasonal Saturday formularies.

rows.articleTitle: Messes de la Sᵗᵉ Vierge le Samedi II de la Nativité au 2 février
rows.selectedSourceObservation: Christmas-to-Candlemas seasonal Saturday BVM Mass reuses the common Marian Saturday introduction, then gives a distinct Introit.

rows.articleTitle: Messes de la Sᵗᵉ Vierge le Samedi III du 3 février au Mercredi Saint
rows.selectedSourceObservation: February-to-Holy Wednesday Saturday BVM Mass reuses the common introduction and supplies Salve sancta Parens seasonal proper.

rows.articleTitle: Messes de la Sᵗᵉ Vierge le Samedi IV Temps Pascal
rows.selectedSourceObservation: Eastertide Saturday BVM formulary reuses the same Saturday-Marian introductory text, not a newly composed commentary.

rows.articleTitle: Messes de la Sᵗᵉ Vierge le Samedi V Temps après la Pentecôte
rows.selectedSourceObservation: Post-Pentecost Saturday BVM formulary has the same introductory panel SHA as four other seasons.
Blessed Alix le Clerc account connects Pierre Fourier's education initiative, first Poussay school and her 1947 beatification.
Blessed Margaret of Lorraine is expressly linked to Nancy–Toul, Verdun and Séez, not a universal feast; source discusses Franciscan Poor Clare life.

rows.articleTitle: Commun d’un Martyr hors du Temps Pascal II : Sacerdótes Dei
rows.selectedSourceObservation: This older Common of a bishop martyr reproduces Parsch Sacerdotes Dei commentary identically to a0048_nouveau.

rows.articleTitle: Commun d’un Martyr hors du Temps Pascal IV : Lætábitur
rows.selectedSourceObservation: This older Laetabitur Common reproduces Parsch commentary identically to a0050_nouveau.
The twelve martyrs are commemorated for an eighth-century Benevento relic translation; the page gives a Mass of their collective cult.

rows.articleTitle: Sts Corneille, pape, et Cyprien, évêque, martyrs
rows.selectedSourceObservation: Cornelius and Cyprian have a shared 16 September Mass and a separately mentioned commemoration of Euphemia, Lucia and Geminianus.
St Nicholas's relic translation is a former Nancy–Toul particular feast with several historical date changes and an account of Bari–Lorraine devotion.
